subject: chemistry_2
question_text: What is an alloy? Give an example.

verification.note: Unit 11 (d and f Block Elements) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", printed chapter 8 ("8. d & f BLOCK ELEMENTS"), book pp.91-94, which prints this question on book p.91 as VSAQ 7. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK EXAMPLE KEPT AND QUALIFIED (book p.91, VSAQ 7): the printed example is "Nichrome - 60% Ni and 25% Fe, 15% Cr". Those figures add to 100 and match a real commercial grade, so they are kept. They are NOT the only nichrome: the widely sold 80% Ni with 20% Cr grade contains no iron at all, so the card writes "a composition", not "the composition". BOOK WORDING SHARPENED: the printed definition says an alloy has "physical properties similar to that of metal"; the card names the properties (conduction, malleability, metallic lustre) so the sentence says something checkable, and adds that an alloy is a mixture with no fixed formula.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
d and f Block Elements — 2 marks

steps.label: Definition
lines: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of a
metal with one or more other metals, or
Its physical properties stay metallic: it
conducts, it is malleable and it has a
An alloy is a mixture and not a compound,
so its composition can be varied.
steps.why: The word homogeneous is what separates an alloy from two metals lying side by side: the components are mixed at the atomic scale, usually by melting them together. Because it is a mixture and not a compound, an alloy has no fixed formula and no sharp melting point, and its composition is quoted as percentages.
common_mistakes: Writing that an alloy is a compound of two metals. It is a mixture, and its composition can be varied.
Leaving out non-metals. Steel is iron with carbon, and carbon is a non-metal.
steps.memory_tip: Alloy = a metal mixed with something else, still behaving as a metal.
steps.margin_note: The word homogeneous and the phrase "properties similar to a metal" are the two marked ideas.

steps.label: Example
lines: Nichrome is about 60% Ni, 25% Fe and
It has a high electrical resistance and
resists oxidation when hot, so it is used
as the heating wire in electric heaters.
Steel (Fe with C) and brass (Cu with Zn)
steps.why: One named alloy with its percentages is what this mark asks for. The three figures add to 100 and match a real grade of nichrome, but they are a composition and not the composition: the common 80% Ni with 20% Cr grade contains no iron at all. Quoting percentages that add to 100 is the part an examiner can check quickly.
common_mistakes: Giving an example with no composition. The percentages are half of this mark.
Naming a pure metal. Copper is a metal, not an alloy; brass is copper with zinc.
steps.memory_tip: Nichrome: nickel and chromium with iron, used as heater wire.
steps.margin_note: Percentages must add to 100. Write 60, 25 and 15 and check the sum before moving on.

insider_note: Two demands, one mark each. A perfect definition with no example is half marks, and so is nichrome named with no percentages.
